description: A solo participant interested in space exploration, web development, and interactive storytelling. I'm creating Relics Beyond, an interactive digital museum exploring NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. My goal is to make space exploration history more engaging and accessible through an immersive, visually rich web experience.
summary:
RELICS BEYOND is an interactive digital museum documenting 19 spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments left behind across the Moon, Mars and deep space. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge's "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, it brings these objects and their mission histories together in three collections.

Visitors can explore individual exhibits, take a guided museum tour, inspect spacecraft through 3D models, discover mission facts, compare spacecraft and explore visualised mission data. The Knowledge Lab adds interactive activities that turn space history into a learning experience.

Using publicly available NASA mission information and imagery, RELICS BEYOND presents the stories, achievements and scientific contributions of equipment that often goes overlooked after a mission ends. It aims to make space exploration history engaging and accessible, particularly for younger audiences.
details:
RELICS BEYOND is an interactive digital museum developed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments left behind during space exploration.

The website organises 19 exhibits into three collections: the Moon, Mars and Beyond. Visitors can explore individual mission exhibits, take a guided museum tour, inspect spacecraft through interactive 3D models, and discover the history and purpose of different pieces of equipment.

Additional features include an Interactive Explorer, an Explorer Passport that tracks visited exhibits, random discoveries, mission timelines, spacecraft comparisons and visualisations of mission statistics. The Knowledge Lab provides interactive educational activities that encourage visitors to test and expand their understanding of space exploration.

The project transforms publicly available NASA mission information, imagery and scientific records into an accessible visual learning experience. Instead of presenting abandoned equipment as obsolete machinery, it highlights the missions, engineering and scientific discoveries associated with each object.

Development: The website was created using Google AI Studio with Gemini-assisted code generation. Its source files use React and TypeScript. The project combines interactive web components, visualisations, 3D viewing features and responsive website design.

RELICS BEYOND aims to make the history of space exploration more engaging and help younger audiences discover the scientific contributions of objects that remain beyond Earth.
